📖 Game script

Seattle's backfield is down to Emanuel Wilson (53+ rushing at −118) and George Holani (+129 to score) with Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price out. Sam Darnold (235+) leans on Jaxon Smith-Njigba (92+, −118 to score). The Seahawks' defense allows 3.8 yards per play. The Chargers are 0–3 and score 14.7 a game: Justin Herbert (200+) has Omarion Hampton (46+, +118 to score), and Ladd McConkey (48+) is questionable, with Brenen Thompson and Charlie Kolar out. Seattle by eight, just past the 7; 40 points, under 42.5.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

SEA: Action Network (Doug Kezirian, "a fluke loss" last week), BettingPros, Sharp or Square, Andrew Erickson (−7) and Mike Florio (Seahawks 27–13). LAC: Steve Fezzik (+7.5) and Brandon Anderson (+7.5; winless teams in Week 4 are 7–0 ATS against over-.500 teams since 2021), plus Steve Makinen and Dave Tuley of VSiN at +7, both best bets. Evan Abrams' primer splits the same way: the winless-team system plays on the Chargers, but Sam Darnold is 12–0 straight up in non-conference games over the last three seasons. Splits: SEA has 52% of spread tickets and 60% of the money, but the LAC moneyline is a big-money flag, 6% of tickets and 22% of the money. The line went from the Action Network open of SEA −6.5 to −7, and the total from 44 to 42.5. At −7 the spread sits on the key number, so the lean is the SEA moneyline as a parlay leg and the under (BettingPros at 43.5, Andrew Erickson at 42.5, and the primer's wind-under system). The projection has Seattle covering by only a point. Card: the SEA moneyline (−319, flagged chalk) sits in the Slot 3 Morning parlay and the Slot 4 Afternoon parlay, and Sam Darnold 2+ passing TDs is in the 7b Afternoon prop stack. The under is left off.

⚠️ What breaks it

Brandon Anderson's winless-team trend hits: Herbert gets a garbage-time touchdown and a backdoor cover inside the 7. With two backs out, Seattle's run game stalls and Darnold turns it over. McConkey playing gives Herbert the target he's lacked.
